real: Why don't we need to prepack A?
prev_agent: For the fp8 `A @ B.T` path, the prepacked layout should be the same physical layout as the current prepacked kernel: `[(K/16), N, 16]`. If `b_t` is the transposed operand with shape `[N, K]`, then: - `packed[kt, n, ki] = b_t[n, 16*kt + ki]` - shape is `[K // 16, N, 16]` - each `packed[kt, n, :]` is one contiguous 16-byte WMMA K-fragment In Python, that is: ```python def prepack_b_t_for_scaled_mm_hip(b_t: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor: N, K = b_t.shape assert K % 16 == 0 return b_t.view(N, K // 16, 16).permute(1, 0, 2).contiguous() ``` That is equivalent to the existing prepack in [hip_kernel_prepacked.py](/home/user_aeefbb67/ComfyUI-FeatherOps/kernel/hip/hip_kernel_prepacked.py#L201), just starting from `[N, K]` instead of `[K, N]`. Why this layout matters: - raw `b_t` stores rows contiguously, so lane `i` reads row `n+i` with a stride of `K` bytes between lanes - packed `[(K/16), N, 16]` stores all `n` for the same `kt` next to each other, so adjacent lanes read adjacent 16-byte chunks - that matches the fast load pattern already used in [hip_kernel_prepacked.cu](/home/user_aeefbb67/ComfyUI-FeatherOps/kernel/hip/hip_kernel_prepacked.cu#L205) So for fp8, “prepacked B for `A @ B.T`” looks like: - not `[N, K]` - not a full transpose buffer - but a K-tile-major layout: `[K/16, N, 16]` If you want, I can add `prepack_b_t_for_scaled_mm_hip()` and a `scaled_mm_hip_bt_prepacked()` path next.
